newsitem.title: CROATIA: UN human rights envoy condemns Mostar violence.
newsitem.headline: UN human rights envoy condemns Mostar violence.

text.p: A United Nations human rights envoy called on Bosnian Croats on Tuesday to remove from power those responsible for Monday's ethnic violence in Mostar, and held the Croatian government responsible for upholding the rights of the town's citizens.

The U.N.'s special rapporteur (investigator) for human rights, Elisabeth Rehn, expressed her "deep regret and sorrow" at shooting in Mostar in which one person was killed and 22 wounded when Bosnian Croats opened fire on Moslem pilgrims visiting a local cemetery.

"...an effort should be made to remove from positions of power those who create tension and attempt to widen ethnic divides, including elements of electronic and printed media," Rehn said in a letter to Kresimir Zubak, Croatian president of the Moslem-Croat Bosnian Federation.

"I am also aware that the authorities of the Republic of Croatia are exercising serious influence in the region and therefore also bear responsibility for the human rights prevailing there," Rehn said.
Zagreb is seen as standing behind hard-line Bosnian Croats in Mostar who seek a separate state in the part of southwestern Bosnia under their control.
